product.olivetti-m24.summary: The desktop that opened Olivetti’s professional range to IBM compatibility, with a 16-bit bus and its own 640 × 400 graphics.
product.olivetti-m24.history: The M24 took Olivetti from the M20’s proprietary environment into the IBM-compatible professional market. Its historical archive places the introduction at Hannover in March 1984; Practical Computing also records its announcement that year. Olivetti developed the machine with its Cupertino group and used AT&T’s channel to sell it in the United States. The M21 brought that architecture to a transportable format. Sources: Olivetti Historical Archive and Practical Computing, November 1984, p. 55.
product.olivetti-m24.warning: The creation profile uses BIOS 1.44. Attach a bootable floppy image to start it.
product.olivetti-m24.technical.configura: The family supports several expansions rather than one fixed configuration. Olivetti documents an initial 128 KB, a 640 KB maximum and an optional 8087; on-board capacity depends on board revision. The 10 MHz M24 SP is distinct from the 8 MHz M24.
product.olivetti-m24.technical.video: Video extends the PC’s graphics capabilities. The proprietary controller combines a 6845 and 32 KB RAM: compatible 320 × 200 and 640 × 200 modes plus monochrome 640 × 400. The optional graphics expansion is a separate board.
product.olivetti-m24.technical.expansion: The expansion adapter accommodates Olivetti and IBM cards. The manual counts seven 62-contact connectors and four additional 38-contact connectors; this 16-bit bus must not be confused with AT ISA. RS-232C serial and Centronics parallel are on-board.
product.olivetti-m24.technical.firmware: Each BIOS consists of two 8 KiB ROMs, with LOW on even bytes and HIGH on odd bytes. Olivetti’s M24/M21 service guide lists 1.43H PQBK and 1.43L PQBL. The preserved 1.43 matches the public copy in DOS Days, which also has 1.21 and 1.36. The available 1.44 originated from a physical M21. A collector later installed it on an M24.
product.olivetti-m24.technical.verified: At 8 MHz and 640 KiB, BIOS 1.43 and 1.44 passed POST and floppy read/write tests. The IRQ1 fix leaves the keyboard buffer empty at cold boot. Pressing Esc returns AX=011Bh through INT 16h. The corrected Ctrl+Alt+Del action restarts both BIOS revisions.
product.olivetti-m24.technical.video_ver: Modes 04h, 05h, 06h and 40h matched the expected pixel patterns with both BIOS revisions. Mode 05h uses the OGC palette and 40h honours the programmable foreground colour. The standard 640 × 400 BIOS mode measured about 25.86 kHz horizontally and 59.87 Hz vertically in BluMach, in line with the reconstructed GO380 cadence.
product.olivetti-m24.technical.disk_veri: With BIOS 1.44, MS-DOS 3.20 partitioned and formatted a 10 MB MFM image on the internal WD1002A-WX1 and booted from C: with A: empty. A test file and the complete image were byte-identical after a hard reset, closing and reopening BluMach, and a separate test of the corrected Ctrl+Alt+Del action.
product.olivetti-m24.technical.limitatio: Video timing validation covers the standard BIOS 40h profile. Custom CRTC settings, physical line doubling in 200-line modes and sync pulse shapes at the connector remain unverified. Other disk geometries and BIOS revisions, RTC persistence and other RAM capacities remain to be tested.

product.olivetti-m24.creation.note: The profile enables internal OGC video and the internal WD1002A-WX1 controller. It creates the machine with an empty floppy drive and no hard disk attached. POST can pause before reporting Fixed Disk Not Ready and booting from A:. Provide the local ROM files and a bootable floppy image. OGC text requires the PQBQ character ROM. The controller availability check requires the WD1002A-WX1 ROM file.
